title: Gemini 4 Carbon leads a new index, and most people cannot use it yet
friendlyTitle: Google's newest model is first on a scoreboard, and most people cannot use it yet
summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on 28 October, two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google says Carbon scores 59 and ranks first on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. The same-day note on Artificial Analysis agrees it is the new number one. Carbon is not in the Gemini app or the public API. Starting this week it goes to a subset of cyber defenders, then to more trusted partners through DeepMind's Fairwind program, while Google takes part in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release testing.
friendlySummary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on 28 October, two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google says Carbon scores 59 and is first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, version 5. Artificial Analysis said the same day that Carbon is the new number one. You cannot use it in the Gemini app or through the public developer service yet. This week it goes to a small group of people who defend computer systems. After that, more trusted partners can get it through a program called Fairwind. Google is also in a voluntary U.S. government check before a wider release.
whyItMatters: The introductory price matches Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input at 95 percent off. After that period, Google says the price becomes $4 and $20. Google also reports leads on tests for finding flaws, checking whether they can be used, and writing fixes, and says those tests were run without guardrails. Those cyber scores are Google's. The practical fact is the gate: this is not a model you can switch to today.
